provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for spring: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 薄紙 usu-gami (#F4F2EE), then 花霞 hana-gasumi (#F4D5D9), then 花冷 hana-bie (#EBDBE5), then 実赤 mi-aka (#AC473E). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 13.9, 5.3, 42.5 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: A graded layering (nioi, 匂): a near-white outer layer (薄紙) over two blossom pinks (花霞, then the cooler 花冷), closing on a deep red (実赤) at the innermost edge. The two pinks are the closest adjacent pair in the set on purpose — a gradation is layers that step, not layers that jump — and they still clear the separation floor. 実赤 is an autumn-tagged entry; it is here as the dark lining a pale spring layering needs, not as a claim about its season. The name is ours (花匂, "Blossom Gradient"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
